advancement.kultivator.tempat.tema_oasis: Defeat the Scorpion King in the ruins of the Buried City.
Pass the Whirling Dance on the Night of the Whirling Dance.
Bring home Si Belang, Bulat Khan's lead camel.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_air_p: The Water Gauge Stone rose four marks in one night! They say %s poured the first water into the sacred pool.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_badai: The tower bell rang three times: a sandstorm! The Jade Gate is shut and the caravans on the road shelter behind their camels.
After a storm the dunes always spit something up: ancient coins, mural shards, sometimes a map tablet. Look for the glint outside the walls.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_kafil: Hear those camel bells? The Great Caravan is passing the Jade Gate. The bazaar will have new wares tonight.
The Great Caravan has unloaded at the caravanserai. For two days goods from the west sell cheaper; hurry before they're gone.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_kurma: Five days in a row %s climbed the palace date palms. The farmers say those hands are as quick as a desert monkey's.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_mata_: The queue at the well is gone. Priestess Shui Lian says the name of %s is carved beside the highest mark of the Gauge Stone.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_mural: The twelfth niche of the Cliff of a Thousand Paintings has a new tale: that of %s. Mo Hua says the eyes are painted with gold leaf.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_perin: The desert pack that harried the caravan road was hunted down by %s. The camels can drink at the outer trough again.
This week's caravan arrived without losing a single sack. Bulat Khan treated %s to three cups of tea.
Another nest in the desert ruins was cleared on the Lord's orders. It was cleared by %s.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_perma: Grandmother Gulnar has woven the Queen's Carpet again, the first in sixty years. %s gathered its materials.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_raja_: The Scorpion King in the ruins of the Buried City has fallen. The weavers are already bidding for its tail for red dye.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_tari_: Full moon! Tonight the dancers whirl on the lakeside stage. Anyone may join, if their feet are quick enough.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_umum_: Never buy water from people outside the walls. The Water Shop's water is blessed by the Temple, theirs comes from camel puddles.
From eleven to three the bazaar is shut. Anyone haggling under a sun that high must be a foreigner.
The Crescent Market's guest traders never haggle. One price, one item, one night. By morning the stall is a heap of cloth.
Someone bought a ruin map at the Crescent Market and sold it again for double at the Money House. The map was fake. The Money House did not laugh.
At the Singing Sand Inn the upper east room is the coolest. The owner keeps it for caravan guards who come home with every camel.
The brass smith in the East Bazaar forges lamps from caravan copper. A lamp that hasn't turned green, he says, may not be sold to a bride.
The desert guards drill with spears every dawn in the barracks yard. Whoever drops a spear cleans the camel trough for a week.
The weaver near the West Bazaar refuses to sell green carpets. Green is the lake's colour, she says, and the lake isn't for sale.
On crescent-moon nights, guest traders from the west open stalls in the West Bazaar. They bring only one item each, but a rare one.
The southern dunes sing when the wind blows from the west. The camel drivers say it's the Buried City calling its caravans.
A sand veil costs fifteen Spirit Stones at the carpet stall. Expensive? Try walking outside the walls in a storm without one.
That young painter, Mo Hua, claims he hears voices from the murals. The old painters laugh, but none will sleep in the seventh niche.
Lord Sha Wuyan never smiles in the hall. But every dawn he prays at the Water Temple, alone, before anyone else is awake.
The hired camels at the palace pen never sink in quicksand. Horses? Three eastern traders' horses have sunk this month.
The tower bell rings three times when a wall of sand shows on the horizon. If you hear it, run to the caravanserai, not the lake: there's no roof by the water.
Camels know a storm before the priests do. If every camel in the field kneels facing east, tie your veil on.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_unta_: Si Belang is home! Bulat Khan laughed so hard his camels started groaning. %s found her behind a dune.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_xie_k: The scorpion hermit was beaten by %s under the noon sun. The city's water veins are no longer drained from below.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_oasis_xie_p: The old exile now sits in the twelfth niche of the Cliff of a Thousand Paintings. They say %s coaxed him home with a flask of holy water.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_oasis_kurma: The farmers paid you with twelve golden dates that restore Qi.
Help with the harvest in the Date Garden five days in a row (talk to the garden's farmers).
The palace Date Garden is short of hands at harvest.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_oasis_mata_: The caravan scattered in the storm. Find Ajun, lost among the dunes.
Defeat Xie Duo in a duel. If he vanishes, Shui Lian can call him with the temple bell.
Follow the Map Tablet to the ruins of the Buried City. Smash or seal (with holy water) the four formation pillars near the Scorpion King's nest.
The Crescent Lake rose four marks and the Night of the Whirling Dance was held for you. The Oasis City calls you Water Bearer.
Meet Bulat Khan at the Great Caravanserai and ride west with the caravan. Protect the camels.
The caravan arrived safely and Ajun found a Map Tablet.
Mo Hua says the seventh mural moves. Read murals 3, 6, 7, 9 and 11 on the Cliff of a Thousand Paintings.
Xie Duo yields and will become the hermit of the twelfth niche.
Return to the Water Temple. Priestess Shui Lian awaits you for the ceremony that restores the lake.
The Water Gauge Stone of the Oasis City fell two marks in a month. Something drinks the lake from beneath the sand.
Bring Priestess Shui Lian's news to Lord Sha Wuyan at the Sand Palace: two marks, one month.
Xie Duo, the priest banished long ago, rises from the sand. Hear his demand.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_oasis_mural: Your tale now graces the twelfth niche, seen by every traveller.
Your mural is finished. See Mo Hua at the cliff.
Mo Hua is painting. Wait three days.
A Mural in the Twelfth Niche
Commission your mural on the Mural Tales screen (50 NB) and pick one deed.
Mo Hua wants to paint your tale on the Cliff of a Thousand Paintings.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_oasis_perin: Defeat 8 desert husks within seven days.
The caravan road is safe again. The palace paid your wage.
Desert husks are harassing the caravan road.
The caravan arrived safely. The palace paid your wage.
Take the guild mission 'Camel Escort' and guard a caravan until it arrives, within seven days.
The Lord asks for a caravan to be escorted to its destination.
Go to a desert ruin and defeat 8 monsters within seven days.
The ruin is safe for now. The palace paid your wage.
The Lord orders a desert ruin cleared of beasts.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_oasis_perma: The carpet is finished. See Grandmother Gulnar in the West Bazaar.
The carpet was taken to the palace. See Lord Sha Wuyan.
Bring Grandmother Gulnar 1 Scorpion Venom Tail and 6 Cactus Flowers.
The Queen's Carpet graces the hall of the Sand Palace again after sixty years.
Grandmother Gulnar wants to weave the Queen's Carpet once more, but its materials are rare.
Grandmother Gulnar is weaving. Wait two days.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_oasis_unta_: Ask Ajun to read Si Belang's tracks in the sand.
Search for Si Belang where Ajun pointed, ride her, and bring her home to the Oasis City.
Si Belang is home. See Bulat Khan at the caravanserai.
Bulat Khan hugged you like a brother. Si Belang leads the caravan again.
Si Belang was never found. Bulat Khan says perhaps she found an oasis of her own.
Si Belang's tracks were blown away by the wind.
Bulat Khan's lead camel bolted in the last storm. Without her, the caravan won't move.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_ajun_kafila: Uncle Bulat says I can sit on the lead camel! Listen, the west wind smells like wet stone. That's the smell of water hiding under the sand. So much water... but something is drinking it.
I don't know. But the wind trembles there, like a camel smelling a scorpion.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_ajun_maaf.m: ...Uncle Bulat says grown-ups are allowed to be wrong too, as long as they say sorry. But don't do it again.
(Ajun steps back.) You... you wanted to hand me over to that scorpion hermit. I heard everything.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_ajun_sapa.a: The west wind doesn't smell of rust any more. It used to taste like iron in your mouth. Now it smells like the lake after rain. Uncle Bulat says that means our city will live a long time.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_ajun_sapa.b: Sand is like camel skin. When the wind passes it leaves wrinkles. Long wrinkles mean a far wind, short wrinkles mean a lying wind. My father taught me... before his caravan never came home.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_ajun_sapa.j: I'm not scared any more. Uncle Bulat says grown-ups can misread the wind too. But... don't stand too close yet, okay?
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_ajun_sapa.k: Once. He taught me to hear the silence between two drops of water. I couldn't. But he gave me dates, so I'll go again!
A golden date! For me? I'll keep the seed. Grandmother Gulnar says if you plant it by the lake, in a hundred years it grows as tall as a wind tower.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_ajun_sapa.m: Shh! Listen... the wind is talking on the backs of the dunes. Today it says someone came from far away. That's you, isn't it?
What else does the wind say?
How do you read the sand?
Here's a golden date for you.
What does the wind say today, Ajun?
Have you ever visited Xie Duo?
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_ajun_temu.m: You found me... I chased a sound into the storm. It sounded like someone crying under the sand. I was so scared.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_ajun_temu.p: When the storm died down I saw this tablet half buried. There's a lake drawn on it and a line to the ruins. Keep it, you're braver than me.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_ajun_unta.b: There! Her tracks aren't gone yet. Si Belang is afraid of storms, so she ran against the wind. Bring her home, okay? Uncle Bulat pretends he isn't sad, but he didn't sleep all night.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_ajun_unta.m: Si Belang? I know her tracks! Her left hind foot drags a little, so the sand always leans. Wait, let me read it...
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_ajun_unta_c: Not found her yet? Don't worry, Si Belang never strays far from the smell of water.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_bulat_khan_: Sandstorms come without knocking, and desert beasts love to bite camels' legs. Protect my camels; if even one falls, the caravan stops. And that child... she likes to run into storms chasing sounds. Watch over her.
So the Lord finally listens! Hah! The caravan is ready: six camels, two guards, and Ajun on the lead camel. We ride six hundred paces west, to where Ajun says the wind 'smells of water'.
Tired, passenger? A camel saddle is the best bed in the desert. Close your eyes; when you wake, we'll be far ahead.
I want to watch the road.
Now Si Belang won't walk unless you're the one holding her rope! That camel is as stubborn as my grandmother. You're a friend of this caravan for life, remember that.

By day the sand lies, by night the stars tell the truth. The Jug Star in the north, the Three Camels in the east. If both vanish behind the dust, follow that little one, Ajun. She reads the wind on the backs of the dunes the way I read my ledger of debts. Hahaha!
Not there. That seat is for people who don't trade children for water. ...Ajun says she has forgiven you. I haven't. Give me time, and give the child some distance.
Storms don't ask permission, friend. What matters is you went back into that storm for Ajun. Camels can be bought again; a child who reads the wind cannot.
Hahaha! A new face in the Great Caravanserai! Sit, sit. My camels stink, but they never get lost. Where are you headed?
Show me the caravan schedule and camel hire.
How do you find your way in the desert?
Our caravan came home whole, Bulat Khan.
I'm sorry about the caravan scattered in the storm.
Hah! Six camels set out, six camels came home, plus one map tablet! Every night I tell it at the teahouse, and every night the storm gets bigger. Next week it'll be as tall as the wind tower. Hahaha!
Camels can be bought, friends cannot! Go, before I have Si Belang spit on you... if only she were here.

Hah... don't look at me like that. I'm not sad. It's just... Si Belang, my lead camel, bolted in the last storm. Twenty years she walked at the head of my caravan. The others won't take a step without her.
Ha! Ask Ajun. If anyone can read Si Belang's tracks in sand the storm has swept, it's her.
SI BELANG! Hahaha! Look at her, grinning as if she never did anything wrong! You, friend, from today you are a brother of my caravan!
She was waiting for me behind a dune.
Golden dates from the palace garden, keep them for a long journey. And whenever you ride with my caravan, your camel walks second from the front, right behind Si Belang!
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_gulnar_baha: Great scorpions nest in the western ruins; treasure hunters come back with a tail, or don't come back at all. Sometimes the guest traders of the Crescent Market sell one. Cactus flowers bloom on top of old cacti in the dunes.
Have you found the materials, child?
Here is the venom tail and six cactus flowers.
Good, good. Two days, child. Two days and two nights, and don't disturb me.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_gulnar_jadi: Look! (The carpet unrolls: blazing red, dawn yellow, and a little scorpion in its corner.) My grandson has already carried it to the palace. Go to the Lord; let him know who found the materials.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_gulnar_ratu: Red from a desert scorpion's venom tail, soaked for seven nights. Yellow from six cactus flowers, picked while the dew is on them. Bring me those, and I'll weave once more before my eyes give out.
Ever heard of the Queen's Carpet? A red that never fades, a yellow like sunrise. My mother wove the last one for the Lord's mother. I still remember how... but the materials, ah, the materials.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_gulnar_sapa: My threads knew first. Wool dipped in lake water takes the red deeper now, like in my mother's day. Healthy water makes honest colours.
The diamond is the spring. The wavy line is the caravan road. And the scorpion at the border is the guardian. My grandmother said a carpet without a scorpion gets stolen by the wind.
Sit on that cushion, child. Don't step on the red thread. A desert carpet is woven in three seasons, sold in three seconds, and used by three generations.
I'd like to see your wares, Grandmother.
Did you hear the lake has recovered, Grandmother?
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_kafilah_bas: We set out after dawn, halt when the heat peaks, and walk again until the stars come out. Passengers pay eight Spirit Stones and may sleep in the saddle. Guards are paid by the guild, but must be ready for desert beasts.
Our caravans carry silk west and jade east. Will you ride along or stand guard?
What is a caravan journey like?
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_mo_hua_mura: You! You saw it too, didn't you? The priest in the seventh mural turned his head at me last night! He moves every time you pass. I'm sure he wants his tale read to the end.

Third, The Water Disciple. Sixth, The Dry Year. Seventh, The Banished Priest. Ninth, The Scorpion Beneath the Sand. Eleventh, The Stolen Water. Read all five on the cliff wall; touch the paint, don't be afraid.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_mo_hua_pesa: Hey... your face belongs on the cliff. Pay fifty Spirit Stones, tell me one of your deeds, and in three days the twelfth niche will show your tale. Every traveller in this world will be able to see it!
Have you seen the twelfth niche? I added a little gold to your eyes. Don't ask why, my hand decided. Here is the first sketch, for you.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_mo_hua_sapa: I've already started! Wait, where's my brush... Anyway, you're in it, standing by the pool with a flask of water. Or a sword. I haven't decided; it depends on which tale sells better at the teahouse.
Oh! You're not... no, you're not the paint buyer. Sorry, I often forget faces, but never colours. Would you like to see the tales on the cliff?
Does the seventh mural still move?
Does the seventh mural still move?
Will the tale of the lake be painted?
Still, since the hermit fell. Sometimes I think his eyes look toward the gate. I repainted his sky in dusk colours so he wouldn't be lonely.
Still since Xie Duo sat down in the twelfth niche. Now I'm painting a thirteenth mural: a hermit pouring water for a young priestess. I don't know yet who pours for whom. Maybe both.
A thousand years of cave painters. Every great caravan, every storm, every hero has a niche of its own. The twelfth niche is still empty... they say it's for the next tale.

Not with mouths! They whisper through colour. The deep blue in the seventh cave, for instance, always feels cold, like weeping water. The old painters say I breathe too much paint. Maybe they're right.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_pedagang.mu: Welcome, welcome! The first price is for fools, the second for friends, the third for brothers. Which are you?
When does the Crescent Market open?
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_pedagang.pa: Every night once the heat breaks, brass lamps light up along the lanes. When the moon is a crescent, guest traders from the west open stalls too: jade, ruin maps, scorpion tails. One item per stall only, first come first served!
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_pelukis.mul: Mind the cliff ladder, the paint isn't dry. Would you like to read the mural tales?
Where do these colours come from?
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_pelukis.war: Red from the red earth of the west, blue from stones the caravans bring from the mountains, gold from gold leaf beaten as thin as a breath. White? White is bone chalk... don't ask whose bones.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_penari.kapa: Every full moon, after the sun goes down, on the stage by the lake. Unless a sandstorm comes; sand in a dancer's eyes is not a pretty show.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_penari.mula: My bell bracelets ring even when I stand still. Do you want to know the secret of the Whirling Dance?
When is the Night of the Whirling Dance?
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_penari.raha: Don't watch the spinning world; watch one point inside your chest. The priests say this dance was once a prayer for the wind to bring rain. Now it brings an audience, and the audience brings coins.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_pendeta.air: Don't just drink it; holy water is for holy things.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_pendeta.mul: Water be with you, traveller. Priestess Shui Lian leads this temple; we only tend the pool and draw from the well.
Ask for the Blessing of the Spring (3 NB).
Buy a flask of holy water (2 NB).
What does a water priest do?
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_pendeta.res: May the water guard your steps beneath the sun.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_pendeta.tug: At dawn we draw the well, in the morning we read the Gauge Stone, in the afternoon we pray by the lake, at night we light lanterns along its shore. A thousand years, every day, without missing one.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_pengawal.ba: The tower bell rings three times, we close the gate, and everyone goes inside. Outside the walls the wind carries sand as sharp as needles. Wear a sand veil, or ask for a blessing at the Water Temple before you set out.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_pengawal.be: Three parts in a hundred of the value of the trade goods you carry in. Have a Desert Pass from the Lord? Just show it, and you pass without paying a single coin.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_pengawal.mu: Halt there. ...Ah, you've already passed the Jade Gate. Very well. Don't make trouble in the bazaar.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_penuntun.mu: (He lowers the cloth over his mouth.) Want to hire a camel? Twelve Spirit Stones a day. Slower than a horse, but it never sinks in quicksand.
Show me the camels for hire and the caravan schedule.
What should I know about camels?
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_penuntun.un: A camel sprints a little, then walks again; don't force it. In a storm it kneels, and you must shelter behind it. Leave it too far behind and it walks home to the pen by itself. Camels are smarter than most of their riders.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_petani_kurm: Look at those trees, heavy with dates. We're short of hands at harvest. Help us pick five days in a row, and the palace garden will pay you in golden dates that restore Qi.
Pick the ones the colour of the evening sun. Come back tomorrow; miss a single day and the count starts over.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_petani_pane: Welcome to the Date Garden. Will you pick with us today?
How do dates grow in the desert?
Feet in water, head in fire, as our ancestors say. Channels from the lake wet the roots, the sun ripens the fruit. If the lake shrinks, this garden is the first to die.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_sha_wuyan_p: Its red will not fade in a hundred years of sun. Take your wage, and tell Grandmother Gulnar: the palace will pay for her thread for the rest of her life.

Grandmother Gulnar has woven the Queen's Carpet again? My mother sat on that carpet when she received the envoys of the Buried City, sixty years ago. I thought the secret of its dye was buried with them.
Scorpion venom tail and cactus flowers. The carpet has arrived at the palace.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_sha_wuyan_s: You stand in the hall of the Sand Palace. Speak briefly; the sun waits for no one in the desert.
I ask for a Desert Pass.
Any orders for me this week?
Tell me about the Buried City.
I take my leave, my lord.
The desert never sleeps. Carry it out, and come back before seven days have passed.
I'll take my leave.
This pass carries my seal. The Jade Gate guards of any oasis will take no toll from you, and caravan guards will hold their spears in a misunderstanding. Do not make me regret it.
Something else.
I'll take my leave.
...I will not be the last lord of this city. That is all you need to know.
Something else.
I'll take my leave.

Once it was greater than this city; its towers could be seen from three days away. In one night a storm buried it. My grandfather said its lake had shrunk before that night, and no one would admit it.
And this city?
Something else.
You offered a caravan child to a scorpion hermit. The lake was saved and I remain grateful for that. But do not ask me to like you. Bulat Khan will not forget it, and neither will I.
Something else.
I'll take my leave.
Caravans come more often. The merchants say our spring sings again. For the first time since I became lord, I sleep soundly.
Something else.
I'll take my leave.
Water Bearer. This hall is in your debt. Sit if you are tired; the water in that cup may now be drunk by anyone.
Any orders for me this week?
How is the city?
Xie Duo now sits on the cliff. You allow it, my lord?
Xie Duo has fallen, my lord.
Why do you look at me so coldly, my lord?
I take my leave, my lord.
The desert never sleeps. Carry it out, and come back before seven days have passed.
I'll take my leave.
This pass carries my seal. The Jade Gate guards of any oasis will take no toll from you, and caravan guards will hold their spears in a misunderstanding. Do not make me regret it.
Something else.
I'll take my leave.

My father drove him out through the Jade Gate for saving the city the forbidden way. I will not repeat my father's mistake. Let the cliff judge him; this hall has judged the wrong people for too long.
Something else.
I'll take my leave.
I ordered his name carved on the Water Gauge Stone, beneath the mark of the dry year. To this lake he was a thief; to my father he was a saviour. Both are true. That is the weight of ruling an oasis.
Something else.
I'll take my leave.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_sha_wuyan_u: (The Lord is silent for a long time. His fingers tap the arm of his chair.) ...So it has begun. My father waited too long. I will not.

Bulat Khan of the Great Caravanserai knows every water vein between here and the Western Sand Sea. His caravan will ride west; go with it. Take the sand-reading child, Ajun. Her ears are sharper than any compass.
Priestess Shui Lian sent you. I can read it in the way you look at the lake.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_shui_lian_d: Xie Duo will not leave before his business is done. If he vanished behind the dunes, I can call him with the temple bell. He still knows its sound.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_shui_lian_f: One flask for each pillar. May the spring guide your steps.

That map tablet points to the ruins of the Buried City. If a formation really drinks our water veins, do not smash its pillars in anger. Pour holy water on them; a sealed formation leaves no wound in the earth.
Give me four flasks of holy water (8 NB).

(The priestess stares at the painted cliff for a long time.) Only a water priest knows how to listen to the water veins. And only one priest was ever driven out through the Jade Gate. I was a child then. He taught me to draw water without spilling a drop.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_shui_lian_m: The Gauge Stone fell two marks in a month. The old tale says the lake of the Buried City shrank too, before a storm swallowed it in one night. Lord Sha Wuyan must know, but he will not hear bad news from a priestess.
I will go before the Lord for you.
This is none of my business.
Wait, traveller. Your eyes are not a merchant's eyes that only count profit. May I ask for a little of your time?
His father ruled in the last dry year. He watched his father ration the people's water while the palace stores stayed full. Since then the word 'dry' may not be spoken in the audience hall.
I'll tell him my own way.
The Sand Palace stands north of the lake. Tell him: two marks, one month. He will understand.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_shui_lian_p: Keep it well. Healers use it for cooling pills, and they say even a wicked formation flinches when it is sprinkled with it.
The Gauge Stone rose four marks. The queue at the well is gone and the children splash again. I wrote your name beside the highest mark; the priests after me will read it.
Can you hear it? The sacred pool sings again. The gate of the Water Temple is always open to you, Water Bearer.
Ask for the Blessing of the Spring (3 NB).
Buy a flask of holy water (2 NB).
Buy four flasks of holy water (8 NB).
How is Xie Duo in his niche?
Do you grieve for Xie Duo?
The water veins that cracked when I smashed the pillars...
Is the holy-water seal still holding?
Bow your head. Water that has walked a thousand years beneath the sand now runs in your veins. The desert wind will not throw you down today.

The drivers who pass by say your seal still glitters on the floor of the third hall. Water calls to water: the formation now returns what it once stole. You taught us that not everything has to be destroyed.

The pillars broke and the veins cracked with them. The priests mend them with prayer and clay every full moon; it will take ten years for the wound to close. Do not regret it. A seal would have left a scar too.
He once taught me to draw water without spilling a single drop. I pray for him at the sacred pool every dawn. You did no wrong; the lake had to be saved. But let me grieve for the priest he once was.

Every dusk I bring him tea. He pretends not to wait, but his cup is always clean before I arrive. For thirty years we called him a thief; it turns out he was only a man too afraid to watch this city die.
kultivator.cerita.tema_oasis_shui_lian_s: Keep it well. Healers use it for cooling pills, and they say even a wicked formation flinches when it is sprinkled with it.
Something else.
I'll take my leave.
Since the second mark fell each family may draw only four buckets a day. Children wait under the blazing sun. I hate to see it, but I would hate a dry well more.

kultivator.kota_tema.oasis.mural.1.teks: Seven thirsty caravan families followed a sand bird into a hollow. At its bottom, clear water shaped like a crescent moon mirrored the sky. They planted their staffs on its shore and swore: whoever is thirsty shall be given water.
kultivator.kota_tema.oasis.mural.10.teks: Desert guards in pointed helmets line the arch of the Jade Gate, spears levelled at a horde of raiders. Above them, the first Lord of the Fort raises the blue and white banner. Not one raider passed the gate that night.
kultivator.kota_tema.oasis.mural.11.teks: The newest mural, its paint not long dry. The crescent lake shrinks from its shores. Beneath the sand, a shadow sucks the water vein through four rune-carved pillars, and at the end of the vein sits a figure in a faded blue robe.
kultivator.kota_tema.oasis.mural.12.teks: The wall of this niche is left bare on purpose, with only a golden frame. The painters say every age leaves one tale worth painting. This niche waits for the next one.
kultivator.kota_tema.oasis.mural.2.teks: A hundred camels knelt at once on the lakeshore, as if bowing. On their backs, silk from the east and glass from the west. From that day the caravan road turned toward the oasis, and the city grew from tents into mud brick.
kultivator.kota_tema.oasis.mural.3.teks: A child named Duo sat by the sacred pool with his ear pressed to the stone. The priests laughed, until he pointed to where a new well should be dug, and its water gushed as high as a tower. He was made the youngest disciple of the Water Temple.
kultivator.kota_tema.oasis.mural.4.teks: The dancers whirl beneath the full moon, their red sashes like flames that do not burn. The wind follows their turning and the dunes begin to sing. That night rain fell on the desert for the first time in a generation.
kultivator.kota_tema.oasis.mural.5.teks: An old caravan master points at the night sky: the Jug Star in the north, the Three Camels in the east. Beneath, golden lines join oasis to oasis, the first map of the Caravan Road, painted from the memory of the camel drivers.
kultivator.kota_tema.oasis.mural.6.teks: The lake shrank to a puddle. Families stand in line at empty wells. In a corner of the mural, the young priest Duo draws a ring of runes in the sand and drives four pillars into the deepest water vein. Water bursts out, and the old priests' faces go pale with fear.
kultivator.kota_tema.oasis.mural.7.teks: The city lived, but the elders called his formation 'a wound in the earth'. Duo was marched to the Jade Gate, his blue robe torn, his name scraped from the temple wall. He looked back once toward the lake before he walked into the desert. The blue feels cold under your fingertips.
kultivator.kota_tema.oasis.mural.8.teks: A sand demon as big as a hill swallowed caravan after caravan. A swordsman with a blade of fire came from the east and fought three days and three nights. The sand beneath his feet melted into glass; that glass is what the East Bazaar sells today.
kultivator.kota_tema.oasis.mural.9.teks: In the halls of the Buried City, a man in a ragged robe gives water to a small scorpion from his palm. In the next panel the scorpion is as big as a camel. In the last, as big as a house, its eyes red as embers.

kultivator.lore.kota_tema.oasis.1: The city stands on the shore of the Crescent Lake, a spring the sand has not buried in a thousand years. The caravans call it the Eye of the Desert: the last door before the Western Sand Sea, where camels drink for the last time and merchants weigh their nerve.
kultivator.lore.kota_tema.oasis.2: Beyond the western dunes lies buried a city that was once greater than this one. In one night a storm swallowed it, and they say its lake had shrunk first. That is why the priests of the Water Temple keep the Water Gauge Stone: when its marks fall, the city prepares for thirst.
kultivator.lore.kota_tema.oasis.3: Since the city was founded, the cave painters have painted the tales of caravans, dancers and heroes on the Cliff of a Thousand Paintings. Twelve niches hold a thousand years of memory, and the last niche is always left empty for a tale yet to happen.
kultivator.lore.kota_tema.oasis.sumber: Source: Dunhuang on the Silk Road; the Crescent Moon Spring (Yueyaquan), a crescent-shaped pool among the Mingsha dunes, which are known to 'sing' when the wind blows and which, it is said, never buried it in sand; the Jade Gate (Yumenguan) and Yangguan, the last posts for travellers heading west. Inspired by the Mogao cave murals and the camel caravans of the Silk Road; town plan, characters, prices and numbers are game design.
